extracted.intended_audience: biomedical researchers applying for NIH grants (K99, R01, DP2, R34, R03, fellowships, admin supplements) seeking practical funding/process advice
extracted.subtask_description: Practical Q&A guidance on NIH grant funding indicators, interactions with Program Officers and Grants Management, administrative status meanings (eRA Commons), JIT and supplemental requests, and decisions about resubmission vs new submission. Focused on interpreting signals and next steps across multiple NIH mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult your Program Officer early
rubrics_metrics.description: Talk with your PO first, as these administrative supplements are discussed internally by program staff, so your PO can tell you whether your idea will be of interest and how best to frame it if so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the PO to vet whether an idea is of interest and to shape framing; POs can advise on appropriate project period length (e.g., 4 vs 5 years) and whether a mechanism is appropriate. If unsure whether to resubmit or change activity code, ask PO before investing effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: PO enthusiasm is a positive signal but not a guarantee
rubrics_metrics.description: If your PO is enthusiastic about your idea, your odds should be good, but it’s still not guaranteed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat PO encouragement as meaningful (they advocate internally) but continue preparing for administrative checks and formal award processing; don’t assume funding until NoA issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret ERA Commons statuses precisely
rubrics_metrics.description: Different eRA Commons statuses mean different things: 'Pending administrative review' refers to GMS/award processing; 'Pending' before Council can mean electronic approval en bloc; 'Council review completed' and other labels have specific operational meanings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn the exact status language used by NIH: 'Pending administrative review' → refer questions to Program Official or Grants Management Specialist; 'Pending' in advance of Council often indicates approval en bloc; inactivity is not necessarily bad (processing delays are common).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants Management Specialist (GMS) is the award-processing contact
rubrics_metrics.description: The GMS knows the award processing status; the PO may not be able to provide detailed processing updates once the application is in administrative review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the status is 'Pending administrative review' contact both PO and GMS; expect GMS to be the primary contact for award paperwork and timing questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact score / percentile relative to IC payline is primary funding signal
rubrics_metrics.description: Your score/percentile is the important data. IC paylines determine likely funding; a score near or within the payline is the main indicator of funding probability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check institute-specific paylines and historical outcomes; borderline scores ('gray area') depend on IC priorities and portfolio balance. Special mechanisms may not have published paylines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resume & Summary of Discussion drive effective rebuttals
rubrics_metrics.description: For one-page rebuttals, focus on concerns raised in the Resume and Summary of Discussion since those reflect group discussion; individual reviewer critiques may not have been updated after the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address the points the SRO highlighted as discussed by the panel; ask your PO if your rebuttal addresses the discussion appropriately. Keep rebuttals concise and targeted to the documented discussion points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use A1 resubmission when Approach is the main weakness
rubrics_metrics.description: If your grant scored well for Significance but poorly for Approach, submit an A1 (resubmission) to get an extra intro page to explain changes made in response to reviewers' comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A1 lets you explicitly point out revisions and can earn 'brownie points' with reviewers. If Significance scores were weak (3-4 or higher), consult PO because Significance is harder to turn around.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance scores are harder to fix than Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: The Approach can be fixed and improved on resubmission, but weak Significance is more difficult to turn around unless the writing or preliminary data were misleading or insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Significance was scored poorly, discuss with PO whether a new application or different study section might be more effective than a resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: ‘Accepted for consideration’ (admin supplement) is only an acknowledgment
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Accepted for consideration' does not mean that your administrative supplement is considered for funding, but simply indicates that your request has been successfully passed along to your institute for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutes vary: some accept supplements before deciding to fund, others accept only once they decide to fund. Don’t interpret 'accepted' as likely funded; ask PO for institute-specific meaning and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: COVID/urgent admin supplements move faster than normal
rubrics_metrics.description: Urgent competitive revisions for COVID work may take just a few weeks for a decision; typical admin supplements vary (regular supplements can take 2–6 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you responded to an urgent FOA (e.g., NOT-AG-20-022), expect expedited timelines and check ProjectReporter or IC announcements for examples of award timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIT (Just-in-Time) requests indicate active award consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Receiving a personalized JIT request (or JIT materials being requested) is a strong signal that an award is being processed or considered; automated JIT notices are not identical to personalized requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit JIT materials promptly; institution (AOR/grants office) must submit JIT items. Be prepared for follow-up GMS questions (Other Support, IACUC, institutional letters).

rubrics_metrics.name: ‘Budget recommended as requested’ is not predictive of funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget recommended as requested has nothing to do with funding probabilities; non-discussed applications can receive the same statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not read 'budget recommended' as assurance of award. Funding depends on score, IC priorities, available funds, and administrative review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Officer advice to wait is usually positive
rubrics_metrics.description: If your PO suggests you wait before resubmission or taking other steps, it usually means they think there is a reasonable chance of funding and they won't risk you missing a submission cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat a PO’s recommendation to wait as a positive sign, but maintain communication and have contingency plans in case funding does not materialize.

rubrics_metrics.name: IC reassignment may indicate other IC interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Reassignment from one IC to another (e.g., from NCATS to another IC) often reflects other ICs' interest and can be good news for funding prospects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask the original PO who to contact at the new IC and whether additional regulatory approvals (IRB/IACUC) should be pursued to speed award processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receiving a NoA naming you PI affects ESI-eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Once you have a NoA naming you as PI, you become ineligible for subsequent awards that require ESI status (e.g., certain DP2 programs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan career moves and submissions with the timing of potential NoAs in mind; notify PO promptly if you are considering accepting an award that could change eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship awards do not go to Council
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships (e.g., F32) do not go to Council for review; their internal processing/timing differs from project grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect different internal timelines; check with PO for institute-specific fellowship decision timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutes may adjust paylines late in fiscal year
rubrics_metrics.description: Some ICs have precedent for moving paylines at the end of the fiscal year; others stick to posted paylines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask your PO about historical end-of-year behavior at your IC; borderline percentiles sometimes benefit from late adjustments but this is not guaranteed.

rubrics_metrics.name: If application placed on administrative hold, contact PO and GMS
rubrics_metrics.description: If your application is on administrative hold, the PO or GMS can explain the situation; the GMS often provides the award processing perspective while the PO can advise on next steps and possible extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If award cannot be confirmed and eligibility is expiring (e.g., K99), ask PO about eligibility extensions or alternatives (different mechanism/activity code).

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond promptly to PO queries about acceptability and other support
rubrics_metrics.description: ICs check with applicants they are considering funding about other funding and whether the applicant would accept the award; quick, clear responses help the IC manage offers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reply rapidly to such queries to avoid being passed over; be honest about other commitments and acceptance intentions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special mechanisms may lack published paylines and use additional factors
rubrics_metrics.description: ICs do not usually provide paylines for special mechanisms (e.g., R61/R33); awards may be based on more than just the impact score and depend on IC priorities and portfolio fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact your PO for how the IC evaluates those mechanisms; expect programmatic considerations beyond numeric score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-submission materials may be slow to appear; contact SRO if delayed
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries into eRA Commons or PubMed (post-submission materials) can be slow; ensure reviewers and the SRO are aware and contact the SRO if the document is not present in time for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work with your AOR and SRO to confirm receipt; late uploads may not be seen by reviewers, so follow up early if timelines are tight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutions submit JIT and other administrative documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Your institution (authorized organizational representative/grants management office) must submit JIT materials and other award paperwork; applicants can upload but institutional submission/approval is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate early with grants management staff to prepare budgets, Other Support, IACUC/IRB documents, and institutional letters (e.g., visa support for K awards).

rubrics_metrics.name: If an IC discontinues a mechanism, discuss alternatives with PO
rubrics_metrics.description: If an IC ends a program (e.g., NINR R34 discontinued), outstanding or future plans must be renegotiated; you may need to apply to other mechanisms (e.g., R01) and the PO can advise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Talk with your PO about next steps if a mechanism is discontinued, including alternative activity codes and what preparatory tasks are expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain transparency with PO about moves or career changes
rubrics_metrics.description: If you plan to move institutions before a NoA is issued, tell your PO ASAP — telling them will not endanger the award and they need early notice to start transfer processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss whether the award can be issued to the new institution or relinquished by the old; early communication prevents delays in activation after a move.
